clinician.trajectory_summary: A male teenager presented with a 7-year history of slowly progressive asymptomatic swelling over the nape of the neck with intermittent discharge of reddish-yellow fluid and difficulty in neck mobility. Initial microbiological analysis of discharge showed filamentous gram-positive bacilli on Gram stain but cultures were negative. Histopathological examination of a neck biopsy identified colonies of filamentous bacteria surrounded by Splendore–Hoeppli phenomenon and suppurative granulation tissue, consistent with actinomycosis. Imaging (contrast-enhanced MRI) revealed extensive infiltrative lesions with intracranial, meningeal, and vertebral involvement. Initial treatment with ceftriaxone and oral penicillin G induced partial improvement followed by relapse. A revised diagnosis of actinomycetoma prompted treatment with intravenous amikacin, oral rifampicin, and cotrimoxazole, followed by oral penicillin G, doxycycline, metronidazole, and prednisolone. This regimen led to a marked reduction in swelling after 4 months, confirming actinomycosis diagnosis and response to therapy.
